text: Every day, you say things worth a fortune.
So AI note-takers exploded. Plaud alone: over two million devices, and a quarter-billion dollars in revenue.
But every one of them ships your voice to someone else's cloud.
Now the backlash is here. Wiretap lawsuits. Biometric claims. IT teams banning note-takers outright.
So the people who need AI the most... advisors, lawyers, executives, clinicians... are locked out.
Here's the gap. Nobody combines four things. Transcription on the device. Redaction before anything leaves. Consent from everyone in the room. And cloud processing you can verify.
An app can only ask for privacy. A phone can enforce it. That's why we're building AlphaPhone.
The microphone lives in a sandbox with no network. Names get swapped before the model ever sees them. And the listening light can't be hidden.
What do you get? An assistant that lives on your phone. It remembers every meeting, drafts the follow-ups, books the calendar, sets the reminders, and shows you a receipt for every action.
Compliance gets a clean record. And IT finally says yes.
The prize? A twenty-nine billion dollar market. A two billion dollar slice we can win first. Starting with financial advisors, who already pay up to two hundred dollars a month for cloud-only AI.
AlphaPhone. AI that works for you, not on you.
